title: Vanishing derivative outside the free coordinates
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, let $J$ be a set of coordinates, and fix signs on all coordinates outside $J$. If $i\notin J$, then the discrete derivative in coordinate $i$ of the function obtained by extending this restriction is identically zero.
hypotheses_covered: $z$ assigns a sign to every coordinate outside $J$
